introduction_markdown: Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board, General Certificate of Education Examination, Advanced Level, 0710 Biology 1, June 2020. Multiple choice question paper. Time allowed: one and a half hours. Answer ALL the 50 questions in this examination; all questions carry equal marks. Each question has FOUR suggested answers: A, B, C and D. Decide which answer is appropriate. Mark only one answer for each question: if you mark more than one answer you will score a zero for that question. Do all rough work in the booklet using the blank spaces.
enonce_intro_markdown:
**Multiple choice questions** - choose the best answer, A, B, C or D.

**Directions for questions 21 to 28:** one or more of the responses (i) to (iv) is/are correct. Choose: **A** if (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct; **B** if (i) and (iii) are correct; **C** if (ii) and (iv) are correct; **D** if only (iv) is correct.

**Directions for questions 42 to 50:** there are two statements. Read through the statements and then choose: **A** if both statements are true and the second explains the first; **B** if both statements are true but the second does not explain the first; **C** if the first statement is true and the second is false; **D** if the first statement is false and the second is true.
incertitudes: Aucun corrigé officiel n'existe : toutes les clés sont déduites par le rédacteur et vérifiées par une seconde passe indépendante. Le sujet est un scan CamScanner de 5 pages, toutes lues ; filigranes et publicités gcerevision.com ignorés ; aucune figure ni tableau de données dans ce paper. La numérotation de la page 2 à la page 5 est continue de 1 à 50 (pas de question manquante).

Défauts d'impression du sujet : Q11 l'option A est imprimée « Diploccocus » (faute recopiée corrigée en Diplococcus) ; Q14 les options sont imprimées « angiostensinogen » et « adosterone » (fautes d'orthographe recopiées telles quelles) ; Q21 l'affirmation (i) est imprimée « in which the evolutionary change occur », sans négation, alors que le sens attendu est « no evolutionary change » (stase) : la clé B reste la seule combinaison cohérente avec (ii) fausse et (iii) vraie ; Q22 formulation « criterion(s) is/are » ; Q36 « producer food chain » n'est pas un terme standard ; Q47, Q48 : texte imprimé légèrement altéré par le scan (« tl e carotid », « Cortic al nephrons ») recopié sans ces défauts.

Clés plus fragiles mais conservées en QCM : Q5 (« edaphic » = facteurs du sol), Q25 (D par élimination : (ii) et (iii) sont fausses ; l'affirmation (i) « requires glycoproteins » n'est pas une exigence), Q33 (seule « Class » contient humains, grands singes et singes parmi les options ; « Order » n'est pas proposé), Q36 (clé C : chaîne parasitaire ; une chaîne à producteur unique, un arbre, donnerait aussi une pyramide inversée), Q41 (allantoïde : D est la meilleure option, mais l'allantoïde sert surtout à stocker les déchets chez les oiseaux), Q43, Q44 et Q47 (choix entre A et B selon la rigueur donnée à « explains »).

Converties en questions ouvertes par le relecteur (clé ou options discutables) : 11, 22, 30, 45, 49. Q11 (aucune option n'est une cellule isolée : Gonococcus se voit en paires), Q22 (C ou D selon que (ii) est accepté ; (iii) est fausse), Q30 (A et D sont la même mutation ; frameshift B probable), Q45 (première affirmation vague, seconde incomplète ; A probable), Q49 (première affirmation vague ; B probable mais A défendable).

questions.enonce_markdown: What is the role of the alcohol fermentation pathway?
questions.corrige_markdown: In alcoholic fermentation pyruvate is decarboxylated to ethanal (releasing $\mathrm{CO_2}$) and the ethanal is then reduced to ethanol by $\mathrm{NADH}$. This reoxidises $\mathrm{NADH}$ to $\mathrm{NAD^+}$. Glycolysis needs a constant supply of $\mathrm{NAD^+}$ (at the triose phosphate dehydrogenase step), so by regenerating it the pathway allows glycolysis to carry on producing pyruvate and a small net yield of ATP when there is no oxygen. Lactic acid is the product of lactic fermentation (option A); no ADP is produced for an electron transport chain, which does not work without oxygen (B); and the $\mathrm{CO_2}$ is released, not used for the light independent reaction (C). **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: It produces ADP for the electron transport chain.
It replenishes $\mathrm{CO_2}$ for the light independent reaction.
It replenishes $\mathrm{NAD^+}$ so that glycolysis can produce pyruvate.

questions.enonce_markdown: Goats are herbivores. What is the trophic level of a goat in an ecosystem?
questions.corrige_markdown: A herbivore feeds directly on producers (green plants), so it is a primary consumer, at the second trophic level. Producers (green plants) are the first trophic level and are called primary producers; there is no such thing as a secondary producer, and a secondary consumer would eat other animals. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The end products of translation are:
questions.corrige_markdown: In translation, ribosomes read the codons of mRNA and join amino acids, carried by tRNA, by peptide bonds. The end product is a polypeptide chain, which then folds to form a protein. Amino acids are the raw materials, not the products; lipids are not made by translation; RNA is the product of transcription. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following carries the code that determines the sequence of amino acids in a protein?
questions.corrige_markdown: The base sequence of the gene is copied during transcription into messenger RNA (mRNA). Each codon (a triplet of bases) of the mRNA specifies one amino acid, so the mRNA carries the code to the ribosome. rRNA is a structural part of ribosomes, tRNA brings amino acids (it carries the anticodon, not the code), and DNA polymerase is an enzyme that replicates DNA. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following factors affect the distribution of living organisms in the soil?
questions.corrige_markdown: Edaphic factors are the factors that belong to the soil itself: its texture and particle size, water content, pH, humus and mineral content, air spaces and temperature. They determine which organisms can live in the soil and where. Climatic factors act through the atmosphere (rainfall, temperature, light), geological factors concern the underlying rock, and biotic factors are the effects of other living organisms. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is true of chordates?
questions.corrige_markdown: Chordates are deuterostomes: the blastopore becomes the anus and the mouth forms later at the opposite end, so the first opening that develops from the archenteron is the anus. Spiral and determinate cleavage and a blastopore that becomes the mouth (protostomy) are features of protostomes such as annelids, molluscs and arthropods. Chordates show radial, indeterminate cleavage. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: The first unfolding of the archenteron forms the anus.

questions.enonce_markdown: Primary succession will occur after:
questions.corrige_markdown: Primary succession begins on a bare surface that has never been colonised and has no soil, such as new volcanic rock or a new volcanic island. Pioneer species (lichens, mosses) start the process. When an existing community is destroyed, for example by fire, the soil and seeds remain and the process is secondary succession. A climax community is the end of a succession, not the start. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: the formation of a new volcanic island.
a fire burns the existing community.

questions.enonce_markdown: A change in the gene sequence from ABCDEF to ADCBEF occurs as a result of:
questions.corrige_markdown: In the new sequence the segment BCD has been reversed to DCB while A, E and F have stayed in place. A segment of the chromosome that is cut out, turned through 180 degrees and rejoined is an inversion. Polyploidy is the presence of extra whole sets of chromosomes, translocation is the transfer of a segment to a non-homologous chromosome, and substitution replaces one base or gene by another without changing the order of the others. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of these processes generates the majority of ATP molecules derived from nutrient metabolism?
questions.corrige_markdown: The Krebs cycle supplies the reduced coenzymes ($\mathrm{NADH}$ and FADH2) and the electron transport chain with oxidative phosphorylation uses them to make about 26 to 28 of the roughly 30 to 32 ATP made per glucose in aerobic respiration. Glycolysis, fermentation and substrate-level phosphorylation make only 2 ATP (glycolysis) or a very small number of ATP. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Krebs cycle and electron transport chain.

questions.enonce_markdown: The variable component of all DNA molecules is the:
questions.corrige_markdown: Every DNA nucleotide has the same deoxyribose sugar and the same phosphate group, which form the sugar-phosphate backbone. Only the nitrogenous base differs (adenine, thymine, guanine or cytosine), and the order of the bases is what carries the genetic information. Ribose is found in RNA, not DNA. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which of the following is a single bacterial cell?

*Options as printed:* A) Diplococcus.   B) Staphylococcus.   C) Gonococcus.   D) Streptococcus.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Bacteria with a spherical shape are called cocci, and the prefix of the name tells how the cells are arranged: Diplococcus cells occur in pairs, Staphylococcus cells in grape-like clusters and Streptococcus cells in chains. Gonococcus is the only name without an arrangement prefix, so it is probably the answer intended by the examiner, but gonococci (Neisseria gonorrhoeae) are in practice seen in pairs, so the stem does not single out one option reliably.

**Intended answer: C (Gonococcus).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: The relatively large size of the mammalian brain allowing for greater learning, association and memory is due to the:
questions.corrige_markdown: The cerebrum (the cerebral hemispheres of the forebrain) is the largest part of the mammalian brain. Its highly folded cerebral cortex is the seat of learning, association, memory, intelligence and conscious thought. The cerebellum coordinates balance and movement, the hindbrain controls basic functions such as breathing and heart rate, and the midbrain relays visual and auditory reflexes. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In genetic engineering, fragments of DNA from different organisms are linked together by:
questions.corrige_markdown: DNA ligase forms phosphodiester bonds between the sugar-phosphate backbones of DNA fragments, joining a gene to a vector (for example a plasmid) cut with the same restriction enzyme and so producing recombinant DNA. Helicase unwinds DNA, DNAse and endonucleases cut DNA. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An enzyme released in response to a low blood pressure in humans is:
questions.corrige_markdown: When blood pressure or blood volume falls, the juxtaglomerular cells of the kidney release renin. Renin is an enzyme that converts the plasma protein angiotensinogen into angiotensin I, which is converted to angiotensin II. Angiotensin II is a hormone that causes vasoconstriction and stimulates the release of aldosterone, which raises blood pressure. Only renin is an enzyme. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following structures can be used for vegetative propagation in plants?
questions.corrige_markdown: A corm is a short, swollen underground stem that stores food and carries buds, and it can grow into a new plant without any fusion of gametes, as in cocoyam. A flower, an anther and an ovary are parts of the sexual reproductive system. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A nerve impulse is usually transmitted from a motor neuron to a muscle by:
questions.corrige_markdown: At the neuromuscular junction the action potential arriving at the motor neuron's terminal opens calcium channels. The entry of $\mathrm{Ca^{2+}}$ makes vesicles release the neurotransmitter acetylcholine, which crosses the synaptic cleft and depolarises the muscle fibre membrane. The signal is therefore carried across the gap by acetylcholine; the action potential travels along the membranes, and calcium triggers the release but is not the transmitter. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The function of bile salts is to:
questions.corrige_markdown: Bile salts, made in the liver and stored in the gall bladder, break large fat globules into tiny droplets (emulsification) without any chemical change. This increases the surface area for pancreatic lipase to act. Bile salts are not enzymes, so they do not digest or chemically degrade fat, and they do not activate pancreatic enzymes (enterokinase and trypsin do that). **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: activate the enzymes in pancreatic juice.

questions.enonce_markdown: A haemoglobin subunit about 150 amino acids long would require a coded DNA sequence that contains how many nucleotides?
questions.corrige_markdown: The genetic code is a triplet code: three nucleotides (one codon) code for one amino acid. The number of coding nucleotides is therefore $150 $\times$ 3 = 450$. (A stop codon, introns and regulatory sequences would add to this, but among the options 450 is the answer.) **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A gas that causes asphyxiation by binding to haemoglobin, thus preventing oxygen from doing so, is:
questions.corrige_markdown: Carbon monoxide combines with haemoglobin to form stable carboxyhaemoglobin. Its affinity for haemoglobin is about 200 times that of oxygen, so it displaces $\mathrm{O_2}$ and the tissues are starved of oxygen. Carbon dioxide is carried partly as carbaminohaemoglobin but binds at a different site and does not prevent oxygen transport in this way; nitrous oxide and sulphur dioxide do not bind haemoglobin. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The innermost layer of the eye is the:
questions.corrige_markdown: The wall of the eye has three layers: the outer sclera (with the cornea at the front), the middle choroid, which is pigmented and rich in blood vessels, and the innermost retina, which contains the photoreceptors (rods and cones). **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The theory of punctuated equilibrium assumes that:

(i) there are periods of time of stability in which the evolutionary change occur.
(ii) evolution occurs gradually within the lineage.
(iii) speciation can occur in a very short period of time and is marked by rapid changes.
(iv) changes occur within the population for long periods of time.
questions.corrige_markdown: Punctuated equilibrium (Eldredge and Gould) proposes that species stay almost unchanged for long periods (stasis) and that most evolutionary change happens in short bursts, during which new species arise quickly, often in small isolated populations. Statement (iii) is therefore correct and statement (i) is correct in the sense of long periods of stability (the printed wording seems to omit "does not" or "no"). Statement (ii) describes gradualism, the view that punctuated equilibrium opposes, so it is false; statement (iv) also describes slow, continuous change. Only (i) and (iii) remain. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
What traditional criterion(s) is/are used to differentiate prokaryotes from protozoans?

(i) Methods of reproduction and motility.
(ii) Methods of obtaining nutrition.
(iii) Number of cells.
(iv) Presence or absence of cell wall.

*Options as printed:* A) (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct.   B) (i) and (iii) are correct.   C) (ii) and (iv) are correct.   D) Only (iv) is correct.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Protozoans are unicellular eukaryotes and prokaryotes (bacteria) are also unicellular, so the number of cells cannot separate them: (iii) is false, which rules out options A and B. Protozoans have no cell wall whereas bacteria have a peptidoglycan wall, so (iv) is a valid criterion. Nutrition (ii) and reproduction and motility (i) overlap between the two groups (both include heterotrophs and autotrophs, both can reproduce by binary fission and move with flagella), so they are weak criteria, and the stem does not make clear whether the examiner accepted (ii). The answer is therefore D (only (iv)) or C ((ii) and (iv)).

**Most defensible answer: D (only (iv)); C ((ii) and (iv)) cannot be excluded.**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which of these apply to hormones?

(i) Large quantities are needed to produce a desired effect.
(ii) They work interdependently with other hormones.
(iii) They are produced in the tissues that they affect.
(iv) Small quantities can produce effects.
questions.corrige_markdown: Hormones are effective in very small quantities, so (i) is false and (iv) is true. Hormones often act together or antagonistically (insulin and glucagon, oestrogen and progesterone, FSH and LH), so (ii) is true. They are secreted by endocrine glands and carried by the blood to target tissues elsewhere, so (iii) is false. The correct pair is (ii) and (iv). **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
T-cells are generally involved in fighting:

(i) cancer cells.
(ii) transplanted foreign tissue.
(iii) viral infections.
(iv) bacterial infections.
questions.corrige_markdown: T lymphocytes provide cell-mediated immunity. Cytotoxic T cells kill cancer cells, virus-infected cells and the cells of transplanted foreign tissue, which is why transplants are rejected. Bacterial infections are mainly dealt with by antibody-producing B cells, phagocytes and complement, so (iv) is not a typical role of T cells. The answer is (i), (ii) and (iii). **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Facilitated diffusion:

(i) requires glycoproteins.
(ii) requires ATP.
(iii) moves substances against a concentration gradient.
(iv) requires a protein carrier.
questions.corrige_markdown: Facilitated diffusion is the passive movement of polar molecules and ions down their concentration gradient through channel proteins or carrier proteins in the membrane. It needs no ATP, so (ii) is false, and it does not move substances against the gradient, so (iii) is false. Statement (iv) is true. Statement (i) is not a requirement (the transport protein does not have to be a glycoprotein). Because (ii) and (iii) are false, options A, B and C are eliminated and only D is consistent. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which of the following organisms have an open circulatory system?

(i) Grasshopper.
(ii) Millipede.
(iii) Crayfish.
(iv) Earthworm.
questions.corrige_markdown: Arthropods have an open circulatory system, in which blood (haemolymph) leaves the vessels and bathes the tissues in a haemocoel: this applies to the grasshopper (an insect), the millipede (a myriapod) and the crayfish (a crustacean). The earthworm is an annelid with a closed circulatory system, in which blood stays in vessels. The answer is (i), (ii) and (iii). **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which of the following statements refer to the codon?

(i) The codon is a triplet of bases on messenger RNA.
(ii) The codon is non-degenerate.
(iii) The codon base pairs with the anticodon.
(iv) The codon is a triplet of bases on the transfer RNA.
questions.corrige_markdown: A codon is a triplet of bases on messenger RNA, so (i) is true and (iv) is false (the triplet on tRNA is the anticodon). During translation the codon pairs by complementary base pairing with the anticodon of the tRNA, so (iii) is true. The genetic code is degenerate (most amino acids have more than one codon), so (ii) is false. The answer is (i) and (iii). **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The following processes release $\mathrm{CO_2}$:

(i) the Krebs cycle.
(ii) alcohol fermentation.
(iii) the conversion of pyruvate to ethanol.
(iv) oxidative phosphorylation.
questions.corrige_markdown: In the link reaction and the Krebs cycle, carbon atoms of the substrate are removed as $\mathrm{CO_2}$ by decarboxylation, so (i) is true. In alcohol fermentation, pyruvate is decarboxylated to ethanal, releasing $\mathrm{CO_2}$, and the ethanal is then reduced to ethanol; so (ii) and (iii) are true (they describe the same step). Oxidative phosphorylation takes place on the inner mitochondrial membrane and uses oxygen to form water, with no release of $\mathrm{CO_2}$, so (iv) is false. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The most studied sex linked trait in man is:
questions.corrige_markdown: Red-green colour blindness is caused by a recessive allele on the X chromosome, so it is much more common in men, who have only one X chromosome, and it is the classic example of a sex-linked trait in humans (haemophilia is another). Cystic fibrosis, the ability to taste PTC and tongue rolling are controlled by genes on autosomes. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which of the following DNA mutations could be fatal?

*Options as printed:* A) Nucleotide substitution.   B) Nucleotide added or deleted.   C) Inversion of part of a nucleotide.   D) Change of one nucleotide for another.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The addition or deletion of a single nucleotide (a frameshift mutation) changes the reading frame, so every codon after the mutation is altered and a completely different, usually non-functional protein is made (often ending prematurely at a stop codon); this is the type of point mutation most likely to be fatal. Options A and D both describe the same thing (a base substitution, which changes at most one amino acid and may be silent, but can also be lethal in some cases such as a nonsense mutation), and the inversion of part of a nucleotide (C) is not a recognised mutation. Because two options say the same thing and any of them could be fatal in some cases, the stem is not reliable.

**Intended answer: B (Nucleotide added or deleted).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: An enzyme is a large organic molecule with a surface geometry that is composed of:
questions.corrige_markdown: Enzymes are globular proteins, polymers of amino acids joined by peptide bonds. The folding of the polypeptide gives the tertiary structure and the specific three-dimensional shape of the active site (the surface geometry). Monosaccharides, polysaccharides and glycerol are not building blocks of enzymes. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: When populations within the same distribution range reproduce in isolation, it is termed:
questions.corrige_markdown: Sympatric speciation occurs when populations living in the same geographical area become reproductively isolated (for example by polyploidy, behaviour or ecological niche differences) and form new species. Allopatric speciation needs geographical separation, so the populations would not share the same range. Directional and disruptive selection are types of natural selection, not speciation mechanisms. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Humans, great apes and monkeys are placed in which of the following taxonomic categories?
questions.corrige_markdown: Humans, great apes and monkeys all belong to the order Primates and to the class Mammalia. Among the options, only Class contains all three. Humans and great apes share the family Hominidae, but monkeys are in other families (Cercopithecidae and Cebidae), and they are in different genera and species. The order Primates would also be correct but is not offered. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of these lights used for photosynthesis has the shortest wavelength?
questions.corrige_markdown: In the visible spectrum the wavelength increases from violet and blue (about 450 nm), through green (about 520 to 565 nm) and orange (about 600 nm), to red (about 650 to 700 nm). Blue light therefore has the shortest wavelength of the four. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following will provide maximum energy to a large population of humans such as in China?
questions.corrige_markdown: At each step of a food chain only about 10% of the energy is passed on to the next trophic level, the rest being lost as heat, in faeces and in uneaten parts. Rice is a producer (first trophic level) and so offers the greatest amount of usable energy per unit area; fish, chicken and birds are consumers at higher levels. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An inverted pyramid of numbers arises when we have a:
questions.corrige_markdown: In a parasitic food chain a single host supports many parasites, which in turn support even more hyperparasites, so the number of organisms increases at each trophic level and the pyramid of numbers is inverted. Predator food chains and detrital food chains usually give upright pyramids. (A chain that starts with one large producer such as a tree, supporting many insects, is also inverted, but the term "producer food chain" is not standard.) **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Macrophages contribute to the body's defence by:
questions.corrige_markdown: Macrophages are large phagocytes that engulf and digest bacteria and other invading organisms (phagocytosis) and then display antigens to T helper cells. Antibodies are secreted by plasma cells, histamine is released by mast cells and basophils, and memory cells are produced by B and T lymphocytes. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is a characteristic of hormones?
questions.corrige_markdown: Hormones are chemical messengers that are effective in very small quantities. They are not needed in large amounts (A), they are not catalysts like enzymes, which are not used up in the way hormones are broken down after acting (B), and they are made in endocrine glands and carried in the blood to distant target tissues (C). **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Large quantities are needed to produce the desired effect.
They are produced in the tissue that they affect.

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following pairs are homologous structures?
questions.corrige_markdown: Homologous structures have the same basic structure and embryonic origin but may have different functions, showing common ancestry (divergent evolution). The bat's wing and the horse's fore leg are both modified pentadactyl vertebrate forelimbs. The wings of insects (butterfly, housefly, cockroach) have a quite different origin from vertebrate limbs and from each other, and bird wings and insect wings are analogous structures with the same function but different origin. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: The wings of a bat and the wings of a butterfly.
The human arm and the wing of a housefly.
The wing of a bat and the fore leg of a horse.
The wings of a bird and the wings of a cockroach.

questions.enonce_markdown: In a biotechnological process, the step requiring the search for a suitable microorganism is known as:
questions.corrige_markdown: Screening is the first step of an industrial microbiological process: microorganisms are searched for in natural sources (soil, water) and tested for the ability to make the desired product. The best strain is then selected and improved. Scaling up increases the volume of the process and downstream processing is the recovery and purification of the product. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A function of the allantois is to:
questions.corrige_markdown: The allantois is an extra-embryonic membrane that grows out of the embryo's hindgut. In birds and reptiles it stores nitrogenous waste and takes part in gas exchange; in mammals its blood vessels form part of the umbilical cord and help to supply nutrients and remove waste. The amnion forms the amniotic cavity (A), the chorion and trophoblast fuse with the endometrium to form the placenta (B), and the yolk sac stores food (C). The best option is D. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: fuse with the endometrium and form the placenta.
store food for use by the developing embryo.
supply nutrients and dispose of waste for the developing embryo.

questions.enonce_markdown:
**First statement:** All xylem cells are living cells which help to transport water from the soil up to the plant.

**Second statement:** Xylem contains two types of water conducting cells, tracheids and vessels.
questions.corrige_markdown: The first statement is false: the water-conducting cells of xylem (vessels and tracheids) are dead, empty, lignified tubes with no cytoplasm; only the xylem parenchyma cells are alive. The second statement is true, since tracheids and vessel elements are the two types of water-conducting cells. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Both statements are true and the second explains the first.
Both statements are true but the second does not explain the first.
The first statement is true and the second is false.
The first statement is false and the second is true.

questions.enonce_markdown:
**First statement:** Perennating organs enable the plants to survive harsh conditions.

**Second statement:** Perennating organs can be used for vegetative propagation in plants.
questions.corrige_markdown: Both statements are true. Perennating organs (bulbs, corms, rhizomes, tubers) store food and survive underground through the dry or cold season, then give new growth. They can also be divided to form new plants, which is vegetative propagation. Propagation is a second function and does not explain the survival of the plant in harsh conditions. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Both statements are true and the second explains the first.
Both statements are true but the second does not explain the first.
The first statement is true and the second is false.
The first statement is false and the second is true.

questions.enonce_markdown:
**First statement:** During spawning both types of gametes are released into the surrounding and fusion is external.

**Second statement:** If the egg is retained within the reproductive system of the female then copulation occurs.
questions.corrige_markdown: Both statements are true. In spawning (fish, amphibians) eggs and sperm are shed into water, so fertilisation is external. When the egg is kept inside the female, the male must place sperm in her body (copulation), so fertilisation is internal. The second statement describes the opposite mechanism and does not explain why spawning involves external fusion. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Both statements are true and the second explains the first.
Both statements are true but the second does not explain the first.
The first statement is true and the second is false.
The first statement is false and the second is true.

questions.enonce_markdown:
**First statement:** Some caterpillars never metamorphosed into butterflies.

**Second statement:** Moulting is determined by the concentration of the juvenile hormone.

*Options as printed:* A) Both statements are true and the second explains the first.   B) Both statements are true but the second does not explain the first.   C) The first statement is true and the second is false.   D) The first statement is false and the second is true.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The likely reading is that both statements are true and the second explains the first. Moulting in insects is triggered by ecdysone, and juvenile hormone determines the type of moult: when its concentration stays high the insect moults to another larval stage, and metamorphosis to the adult occurs only when its concentration falls. A caterpillar that continues to produce juvenile hormone (or is treated with it) therefore stays a larva and never becomes a butterfly (or moth). However the first statement is vague (many caterpillars become moths, not butterflies) and the second is incomplete, so the question is not reliable.

**Intended answer: A (Both statements are true and the second explains the first).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown:
**First statement:** An epistatic gene suppresses the effect of a gene found only on the same locus.

**Second statement:** An epistatic gene can also be known as inhibiting gene because of its effect on the hypostatic genes.
questions.corrige_markdown: The first statement is false: epistasis is an interaction between genes at different loci in which the allele of one gene masks or suppresses the expression of alleles of another gene (the hypostatic gene); alleles at the same locus show dominance, not epistasis.
